title: Alert fatigue mitigation and observability governance playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects pragmatic patterns and a lightweight governance process to reduce alert noise and make our observability signals actionable. Focus is on inference runtime alerts (hosted + dedicated), model fallback paths, and observability dashboards that feed on-call decisions.

Background / why this matters:
- Oncall bandwidth is saturated; many alerts are duplicates or low-actionability.
- We ship new models and routing policies frequently; metrics drift and alert false positives increase after rollouts.
- We need a repeatable process to define who owns a metric, how alerts translate to runbooks, and how dashboards support quick triage.

High-level goals (measurable):
1) Reduce pager noise: decrease actionable-pager count by 35% across inference services in Q1 (baseline = avg weekly pages, Oct 2025).
2) Improve MTTR for high-severity inference incidents to < 18 minutes.
3) Ensure every critical alert has an owner and a playbook link.

Principles (short):
- Alert = an explicit instruction: what to check first and who to notify.
- Prefer fewer high-precision alerts > many noisy thresholds.
- Metric owners are the gatekeepers for alert creation/modification.
- Dashboards are for triage, not full analysis — include a 3-step drilldown path.

Alert taxonomy (suggested):
- Priority P0 (service down or data loss): SLO burn > 90%/5m, model-serving process crash loop, NVidia GPU OOMs impacting > 10% capacity.
- Priority P1 (severe degradation): P50 latency spike or increase in generation error rate > 5% absolute vs baseline, KV cache corruption errors.
- Priority P2 (investigate / action within 4 hours): gradual SLO drift, queue growth on edge routers.
- Info (no page): metric anomalies for engineering dashboards, capacity planning signals.

Signal definitions (concrete examples):
- token_generation_error_rate: count(errors) / count(inference_calls) over 1m window; alert when > 0.05 for 5m AND model_version != fallback. Owner: serving-runtime.
- prefix_kv_cache_miss_rate: kv_miss / kv_lookups over 10m; alert at > 20% for 15m if traffic pattern is stable. Owner: runtime-cache.
- end_to_end_95th_latency_ms: 95th latency (client->response) over 1m; alert when > configured SLO threshold AND sustained over 3m. Owner: platform-routing.

Dashboard / triage pattern (3-click flow):
1) Summary widget: top 5 signals by cardinality (model, region, route) for the alert window.
2) Breakdown by route/model: heatmap (latency / error rate) with capacity bars.
3) Trace-link + recent rollout info: provide direct link to sample traces and to the PR/rollout that changed model routing in last 24h.
Notes: include a small "what I checked" checklist on dashboards (checkbox UI if supported).

Tracing correlates for alerts:
- When token_generation_error_rate spikes, enrich traces with: model.version, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, kernel_mode flags.
- Add a fast span anchor in front of the runtime runner that tags "policy_decision" (why request was routed to model X). This is critical to separate routing regressions from runtime regressions.
- Sampling: When P1/P0 alerts fire, enable burst sampling for 30m for the affected route + caller_id. Otherwise keep adaptive 0.5% baseline sampling for production inference.

Sampling and retention policy (proposal):
- Baseline traces: 0.5% of requests, 7d retention for full spans.
- Alert-triggered burst: 100% sampling for affected trace keys for 30m, store minimal spans for 30d (for postmortem).
- High-cardinality debug snapshots stored off-cluster (S3) and referenced in dashboards.

Runbook template (per alert):
- TL;DR (1 line): what to do immediately.
- How to check: top 3 queries/dashboards + trace quick-links.
- Escalation: who to call after 12 minutes (name + slack handle).
- Mitigation steps: fallback to safe model, toggle route to dedicated infra, scale-up steps.
- Postmortem checklist: collect traces, confirm rollback state, update alerts.

Metric ownership + governance process:
- Every metric must have an owner in metadata (teams/individual). Owners review alerts quarterly.
- New alert creation workflow: PR in observability repo -> automated lint (checks: owner set, runbook link present, SLO mapping, test-case for false-positive simulation) -> peer review by oncall lead -> merge + 24h quiet period.
- Quarterly audit: a 2-hour "alert spring-clean" where owners run the noisiness report (top 20 noisy alerts), remove or reduce thresholds.

Implementation notes / quick wins:
- Add owner and runbook fields to metric catalog (Confluence + metric registry).
- Create an "alert lint" GH action that enforces metadata and rejects alerts without runbooks.
- Build a dashboard template with the 3-click triage flow and a small "observability checklist" widget.
- Start with 5 critical alerts to pilot sampling bursts and dashboard drill paths.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- What's the acceptable baseline sampling cost? (estimate cost vs. diagnostic value)
- Should alert bursts persist across related routes (fan-out) or be strictly per-route?
- How do we surface model-quality correlated signals (LLM hallucination proxies) in runtime alerts?

Next steps / TODOs:
- Diego: prototype alert-lint GH action (owner: Diego) — due 2026-01-12.
- Priya: wire dashboard template and add trace quick-link widget — due 2025-12-15.
- Maya: prepare pilot list of 5 alerts and schedule "alert spring-clean" for Jan 2026.
- Connor: estimate trace storage cost for burst policy by 2025-12-01.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally light-weight; want fast iteration. Expect a couple of cycles. Add comments inline or propose changes in linked Confluence doc.
- If you add an alert, please add the owner tag and a one-paragraph runbook before merging.

-- end --
